prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make ONE production icon atlas for Elements - Icons. The supplied image is a STYLE REFERENCE; replace its subjects with the subjects specified here.
Rustic, earnest old-fashioned COLOURED WOODCUT. Match the supplied references' warm black, dull ochre, clay/rust red, slate blue, muted olive and creamy carved cuts, but visibly simpler and less polished than the first reference: a small number of broad confident cuts, occasional knife slips, uneven angular contours, slightly crooked handmade things, thin missed patches in ink and colour plates shifted slightly beyond or short of their black outlines. Imperfect registration must look printed, not blurred. No smooth gradients, modeled digital shading, tiny decorative hatching, glossy highlights, outline stickers, cute toy proportions, circular badges, frames or presentation shadows. Humble functional objects, easily recognised at 56 pixels. Natural, clear silhouettes before texture. Transparent outside each object.
EXACTLY FIVE columns and FOUR rows, 20 equal cells, wide 5:4 atlas. Keep every complete subject centered in its own cell with at least 15% TRANSPARENT MARGIN from all cell boundaries; strict grid with clear wide gutters. No labels or numbering, no drawn grid, no text except where explicitly requested. Do not repeat objects from the reference unless listed. Make the states of related objects clearly different, using silhouettes and visible contents.
READING ORDER:
1. Fish: One ordinary whole slate-blue river fish in side view, visible tail and fins, no smoke
2. Brine: Shallow glazed bowl dominated by slate-blue WATER with a small angular white salt crust on its rim; salt crystals, not shells
3. Smoke: Three dark blue-grey curling rising smoke columns above a few smouldering embers, no bright flame
4. Vinegar: Narrow-necked plain brown cruet with a cork beside it and a small pale cloudy liquid surface visible in a little cup, no apple garnish
5. Pickles: Small open bowl of recognisable red and green fruit wedges in amber pickling liquid, no jar
6. Washstand: Plain waist-high wooden table with a large blue-glazed washing basin, no soap
7. Covered water jar: Glazed ochre water jar with fitted wooden lid, a little blue water showing at the edge and a blue drop painted on its side
8. Filter bed: Shallow wooden tray with a visible upper layer of ochre sand and lower layer of black charcoal, no pipe
9. Water filter: Short upright hollow wooden pipe containing visible sand/charcoal layers in a cutaway, water dripping from the bottom
10. Filtered water: Plain glass cup of pale blue water with a tiny filter-bed silhouette beside it, no steam or fire
11. Boiled water: Small blackened cooking vessel of blue water with three steam strokes and visible large boiling bubbles
12. Drinking-water bowl: Plain shallow blue-glazed bowl full of clear blue water beside a small wooden drinking cup, no salt or reed
13. Wash station: Same wooden washstand and large blue basin, now with a cream soap bar and hanging clean cloth
14. Soap: One irregular cream soap bar, three small broad outlined bubbles beside it
15. Ash: Low powdery pale grey ash pile with one partly burned twig, no intact black charcoal sticks
16. Lye: Plain small dark mixing crock of cloudy pale liquid with a wooden stirrer and grey ash beside it, no bubbles or soap bar
17. Stove: Plain squat brick cooking stove with a dark iron top and one inset pot, small fire opening below
18. Iron-handled cooking pot: Deep ochre pottery cooking pot with a large arched dark iron bail handle and blackened base
19. Feast table: Long simple trestle table set with a loaf, two large food bowls, apples and three cups, no patterned cloth
20. Drying rack: Simple wooden upright frame strung with open rope netting, EMPTY, no fish or fruit
Keep all twenty separate, complete and rustic.
